clusters.headline: Bomb discovered at Peoria, Illinois ethanol plant prompts mandatory evacuations
clusters.summary: Authorities discovered a bomb at the BioUrja Renewables ethanol plant in Peoria, Illinois, on Friday, triggering a mandatory one-mile evacuation zone. The evacuation order affected residents and businesses in both Peoria and the adjacent municipality of East Peoria. While bomb technicians rendered the initial device safe on Friday evening, police and the FBI continue to search the facility for additional threats. Peoria Mayor Rita Ali and Police Chief Brad Dixon confirmed the device was a credible threat, and the evacuation order remained in place as of Saturday.
key_facts: The device was found at the BioUrja Renewables plant on Southwest Washington Street.
Peoria Mayor Rita Ali stated, 'We know that it is a real threat. We know it is a bomb.'
The evacuation zone covers a one-mile radius around the facility.
Bomb technicians rendered the device safe at approximately 9:12 p.m. local time on Friday.
Congressman Eric Sorensen warned residents that officials could not guarantee the safety of the city.
clusters.outlet_disagreement: The Daily Mail uses more sensationalist language, such as 'Panic' and 'active bomb,' compared to the more neutral reporting from AP and The New York Times.

clusters.headline: FAA Lifts Nationwide Ground Stop Following Widespread Flight Disruptions
clusters.summary: The Federal Aviation Administration issued a nationwide ground stop that halted all departing flights across the United States due to technical communication issues. The disruption affected air traffic control systems, leading to thousands of flight cancellations and delays. While the FAA has since lifted the order, significant travel disruptions are expected to persist. Aviation tracking data indicates that over 13,000 flights were impacted by the event.
key_facts: Transportation Secretary Sean Duffy cited a communication issue impacting all Air Route Traffic Control Centers.
This event marks the third time all departing flights have been grounded in the US.
Previous nationwide ground stops occurred on September 11, 2001, and in January 2023.
FlightAware reported that over 13,000 flights were delayed or canceled.
The FAA's ground stop order was issued on a Friday.
clusters.outlet_disagreement: While most outlets report over 13,000 total disruptions, the TASS report cites lower figures of approximately 7,000 total delays and cancellations.

clusters.headline: Democrat Mary Peltola extends lead over Republican Dan Sullivan in Alaska Senate race
clusters.summary: Democrat Mary Peltola has extended her lead over Republican incumbent Senator Dan Sullivan in the Alaska U.S. Senate race as ballot counting continues. Following the counting of over 20,000 additional ballots on Friday, the total number of tallied votes surpassed 279,000. Peltola currently holds 49.8% of first-choice votes compared to 46.1% for Sullivan. While Peltola's campaign has declared victory, the race remains officially uncalled by major news outlets.

clusters.headline: United States Loses Measles Elimination Status After 26 Years
clusters.summary: The Pan American Health Organization (PAHO) has revoked the United States' measles-elimination status after determining the country failed to halt continuous transmission of the virus for over a year. This decision ends a 26-year period during which the U.S. was considered measles-free. Reports indicate the country is currently facing its highest number of measles cases in over three decades, with figures ranging from 5,412 to 7,500 confirmed cases in 2026. The surge is attributed to declining vaccination rates, policy changes, and staff cuts.
key_facts: The U.S. achieved measles-free status in 2000.
The MMR vaccine is 97% effective after two doses.
CDC data reports 5,412 confirmed cases in 2026, the highest since 1991.
Outbreaks have been specifically noted in Utah, Pennsylvania, New York, and Wisconsin.
The decision was based on evidence that a single strain circulated uninterrupted for 12 months.
clusters.outlet_disagreement: While most outlets report the case count as 5,412, The Hindu cites a higher figure of 7,500 infections and 13 deaths, and TASS highlights specific November death locations not mentioned in other reports.

clusters.headline: Vice President JD Vance weighs skipping 2028 presidential race following midterm losses
clusters.summary: Following significant Republican losses in the November 3 midterm elections, Vice President JD Vance is reportedly reconsidering his potential candidacy for the 2028 presidential race. Reports indicate that Vance is uncertain about his future as the leader of the MAGA movement due to internal party divisions and the political fallout from the war with Iran. While he has not made a final decision, advisers suggest he is weighing his personal ambitions against the challenging political climate created by Donald Trump. Other prominent Republicans are also beginning to explore potential 2028 bids as the party navigates its recent electoral defeats.
key_facts: Republicans lost their majorities in both chambers of Congress in the midterm elections.
Vance is facing criticism for blaming the Iran war for the party's election defeats.
Interviews with approximately a dozen people close to Vance suggest he is uncertain about a 2028 run.
Vance's deliberations include concerns over whether any Republican can win in the current political climate.
clusters.outlet_disagreement: While most outlets report Vance is considering skipping the race, The Washington Post frames his candidacy as still likely despite the reported internal doubts.

clusters.headline: Mayor Zohran Mamdani and President Trump Agree to 90-Day SNAP Rule Delay
clusters.summary: New York City Mayor Zohran Mamdani has secured a 90-day extension for small retailers nationwide to comply with new Supplemental Nutrition Assistance Program (SNAP) food-stocking requirements. The agreement, reached following discussions with President Donald Trump and Agriculture Secretary Brooke Rollins, delays the original November 4 deadline. The new USDA guidelines require stores to stock at least seven varieties of items within four staple food categories: dairy, grains, protein, and fruits or vegetables. The extension takes effect on Friday and aims to prevent small businesses, such as bodegas and corner stores, from losing their ability to accept food stamps.
key_facts: The extension period is 90 days.
The original compliance deadline was November 4.
New rules require seven varieties in each of four staple food categories.
Agriculture Secretary Brooke Rollins participated in the discussions.
Mayor Mamdani had previously requested a six-month postponement from the USDA.

clusters.headline: House Minority Leader Hakeem Jeffries Heckled at Democratic Conference in Denver
clusters.summary: US House Minority Leader Hakeem Jeffries was repeatedly heckled by protesters during the Democratic Party's 'What's Next' conference in Denver, Colorado, on Friday, November 13, 2026. The protesters interrupted his speech to demand more progressive policies, including the Green New Deal and Medicare-for-all, while accusing him of being too timid regarding the cost of living. The event, which included other Democratic officials like Ro Khanna and Chris Van Hollen, was intended to strategize for the party's upcoming control of Congress in January 2027. Approximately 10 hecklers participated in the disruption, highlighting ongoing ideological divisions between moderates and progressives within…

Protesters shouted, 'When is it time for a Green New Deal?' and 'When is it time for Medicare-for-all?'
The event was moderated by political consultant Jessica Tarlov.
Approximately 10 hecklers were involved in the disruption.

clusters.headline: Chicago Chief Financial Officer Ashlee Gabrysch Resigns After Three Months
clusters.summary: Chicago Chief Financial Officer Ashlee Gabrysch resigned on Friday after serving in the role for only three months. In her resignation statement, Gabrysch cited an inability to provide complete and accurate financial information without compromising her professional integrity. Her departure marks the third time the city has lost a CFO within a single year. The resignation has prompted calls for an investigation and raised concerns regarding the city's credit rating during a contentious budget season.
key_facts: Ashlee Gabrysch is the third person to hold the Chicago CFO position in less than a year.
Gabrysch served in the role for three months before resigning.

clusters.headline: Former Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang resigns following reports of multiple extramarital affairs
clusters.summary: Jensen Huang resigned as CEO of Nvidia on November 12, 2026, following revelations of multiple extramarital affairs. Reports indicate Huang misled company leadership, including general counsel Tim Teter and CMO Alison Wagonfeld, by characterizing his relationship with Alice Huang as standard business dealings. Alice Huang is a Singapore-based executive suspected by U.S. intelligence of being a Chinese spy. Following the scandal and an independent probe by Wachtell, Lipton, Rosen & Katz, Nvidia shares have declined by more than 30%.
key_facts: Jensen Huang resigned as Nvidia CEO on November 12, 2026.
Alice Huang is an executive at the Singapore-based company Megaspeed.
Nvidia hired the law firm Wachtell, Lipton, Rosen & Katz for an independent investigation.
Nvidia shares have fallen more than 30% amid the scandal.
Jensen Huang is 63 years old.
clusters.outlet_disagreement: While most outlets focus on the corporate governance and security implications of the affairs, the Daily Mail emphasizes the personal emotional state of the former CEO and his alleged workplace conduct toward his successor.

clusters.headline: FAA nationwide ground stop causes widespread flight disruptions across the United States
clusters.summary: A nationwide FAA ground stop halted departing flights across the United States for over four hours on Friday. The outage, which affected 22 regional air traffic control centers, impacted more than 1.5 million passengers. Sports teams in the NBA, NHL, and college football were among those stranded, leading to significant travel chaos. The FAA lifted the ground stop at 8:15 p.m. Eastern time, though airlines warned that recovery from the resulting delays could take days.

The FAA lifted the stop at 8:15 p.m. Eastern time on Friday.

clusters.headline: Trump administration delays enforcement of Medicaid work requirements by six months
clusters.summary: The Trump administration has granted states a six-month delay in enforcing new work requirements for Medicaid recipients. While the policy technically begins on January 1, the Centers for Medicare & Medicaid Services issued guidance stating that states will not be held accountable for enforcement until July 1. This decision follows concerns from healthcare advocates and state officials regarding the rapid pace of the rollout. The policy was previously a central component of the administration's healthcare agenda.

The new deadline for state accountability is July 1.

clusters.headline: Secretary of State Marco Rubio Criticizes International Criminal Court in Federalist Society Speech
clusters.summary: U.S. Secretary of State Marco Rubio delivered a speech to the Federalist Society in Washington on November 13, 2026, where he criticized the International Criminal Court (ICC) and international law. Rubio argued against allowing international institutions to restrain U.S. foreign policy, labeling them tools of elites. During the address, he also discussed the U.S.-Israeli conflict with Iran, stating the goal is to prevent Tehran from developing nuclear weapons. The speech marks his first major public remarks following the Republican midterm election losses on November 3.

clusters.headline: SpaceX Starship reaches orbit but aborts booster recovery attempt
clusters.summary: SpaceX successfully launched its 124-meter Starship rocket from Starbase, Texas, for its 15th test flight on Friday. While the spacecraft reached Earth's orbit and deployed 26 Starlink satellites, an unspecified malfunction forced the company to abort the planned mid-air recovery of the Super Heavy booster. Instead of the intended catch, the booster was diverted to an offshore splashdown. The mission aimed to achieve a groundbreaking twin capture of both rocket components.

The mission involved the deployment of 26 Starlink satellites.
The launch took place at Starbase in southern Texas.

The order, which cited extraordinary circumstances and safety concerns, resulted in the delay of over 8,500 flights and the cancellation of nearly 8,000 others. The ground stop was lifted on Friday evening after lasting several hours. Officials confirmed there was no indication of an attack and that all passengers remained safe.
